intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Temple Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent 12th-century Khmer temple complex at sunrise, wandering through Angkor Wat, Bayon, and Ta Prohm. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day guided circuit covering the most iconic temples and learning about the ancient Khmer Empire's history and spiritual traditions.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Historical & Cultural Immersion
experiences.description: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda to admire Khmer architecture and Buddhist artifacts, followed by a sobering but essential visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Choeung Ek Memorial to understand Cambodia's modern history. End with a sunset stroll along the Tonle Sap and Mekong riverfront promenade.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine island of Koh Rong Samloem and spend the day on Saracen Bay or Lazy Beach, two of Cambodia's most stunning and unspoiled white-sand beaches. Snorkel in crystal-clear turquoise waters, spot bioluminescent plankton at night, and enjoy fresh seafood at a beachside shack.

experiences.name: Siem Reap Khmer Cooking Class & Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Khmer cooking class starting with a guided tour of the vibrant Phsar Leu local market to source fresh ingredients like lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and mango salad, then enjoy your creations with fellow travelers.
experiences.location: Old Market Area (Phsar Chas), Siem Reap

experiences.name: Kampot River & Pepper Plantation Exploration
experiences.description: Cruise along the serene Kampot River by kayak or longtail boat, passing French colonial architecture and lush jungle scenery. Visit a world-renowned Kampot pepper plantation for a guided tour and tasting, then explore the charming riverside town on foot, sampling local street food and fresh durian at the night market.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange a budget tuk-tuk or shared shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a nearby convenience store or 24-hour street food stall near the resort if available — budget $2–4 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to save money. Negotiate tuk-tuk fare before boarding — expect $8–15 USD depending on distance. Keep some USD or Khmer Riel handy. Cambodia widely accepts USD.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a relaxed wake-up, explore the beachfront area around Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a morning stroll along the beach, enjoy the coastal scenery, and get oriented with the local neighborhood. Visit a local market nearby to pick up snacks and essentials.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or take a cheap tuk-tuk to explore the nearest town. Visit local temples (wats) in the area for a taste of Cambodian Buddhist culture. Explore colorful street murals and local craft stalls. If near Sihanoukville or Kep, explore the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for a stunning sunset. Head to a local beachside restaurant or food shack for a relaxed dinner. Enjoy the laid-back coastal atmosphere and chat with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local bakery — try Khmer rice porridge (Bobor) for $1–2 USD
meals.lunch: Local Khmer restaurant in town — Lok Lak (stir-fried beef with rice) or noodle soup for $2–4 USD
meals.dinner: Beachside seafood shack — grilled fish or squid with rice for $4–6 USD

day_by_day.notes: November is the start of the dry season in Cambodia — expect warm sunny weather, ideal for beach days. Stay hydrated. Exchange a small amount of money at a local bank or ATM for Riel for small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning budget bus or shared minivan toward Phnom Penh (Cambodia's capital). Book tickets in advance for $6–10 USD. Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way. Arrive in Phnom Penh by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — entrance fee around $6.25 USD. Marvel at the stunning Khmer architecture, gilded spires, and the famous Emerald Buddha. Stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the bustling Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for souvenir shopping and local snacks. Explore the vibrant street food scene along the riverfront. Return to resort or book a budget guesthouse in Phnom Penh for $8–15 USD if staying overnight.

meals.breakfast: Bus station snack or Khmer bread with pâté (Num Pang sandwich) — $1 USD
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Royal Palace — Amok (fish curry in coconut) with rice for $3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Riverside street food stalls — grilled corn, spring rolls, and noodles for $3–5 USD

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Penh is approximately 4–5 hours from coastal areas by bus. Book bus tickets the day before from a local guesthouse or online. Dress modestly when visiting the Royal Palace — shoulders and knees must be covered.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — entrance $3 USD. This powerful and sobering historical site documents the Khmer Rouge regime. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit. This is one of Cambodia's most important historical landmarks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — $3 USD entrance, approximately 15 km from the city center. Rent an audio guide ($3 USD) for a deeply informative experience. Pay respects at the memorial stupa filled with victims' skulls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and explore the lively Bassac Lane bar and café street for budget drinks and street food. Visit the night market along the Mekong riverfront. Enjoy a relaxing evening reflecting on the day's historical experiences.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café — fried rice or baguette with eggs for $1.50–3 USD
meals.lunch: Local eatery near Tuol Sleng — Khmer curry or fried noodles for $2–4 USD
meals.dinner: Night market or riverside restaurant — BBQ skewers, fresh spring rolls, and local beer for $4–6 USD

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng Museum and Killing Fields are emotionally heavy experiences. Take your time and be respectful. Photography is allowed in most areas but be mindful of the solemn nature of the sites. Tuk-tuk to Choeung Ek costs about $10–12 round trip — negotiate before going.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget bus or shared minivan from Phnom Penh to Siem Reap — approximately 5–6 hours, costing $6–10 USD. Book with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for reliability. Enjoy the rural Cambodian landscape along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siem Reap and check into a budget guesthouse near Pub Street — dorms from $4–6 USD, private rooms from $10–15 USD. Freshen up and take a tuk-tuk to the Angkor National Museum ($12 USD) for an excellent introduction to Angkor Wat's history and the Khmer Empire before tomorrow's temple visit.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Pub Street and Old Market (Phsar Chas) area. Browse local handicraft stalls, try street food, and soak in the lively atmosphere. Watch traditional Apsara dance performances — some restaurants offer free shows with dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bus station or guesthouse — Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) for $1.50 USD
meals.lunch: Roadside stop during bus journey — packed snacks or $2 rice dishes
meals.dinner: Pub Street area restaurant — try a set Khmer meal with Amok, spring rolls, and rice for $4–7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book your Angkor Wat temple pass in advance or first thing tomorrow morning. A 3-day pass costs $62 USD and is well worth it. Siem Reap is very budget-friendly with plenty of $1 draft beer and cheap local eateries.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before dawn (4:00–4:30 AM) and hire a tuk-tuk ($15–20 USD for the day) to Angkor Wat for the iconic sunrise over the temple — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Explore Angkor Wat's outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting Hindu mythology, and the central towers. Allow 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex — visit the Bayon Temple with its famous smiling stone faces, the Baphuon, Elephant Terrace, and Leper King Terrace. Have lunch at a local stall inside the Angkor complex. Visit Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider temple') where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap, shower and rest. Head to the Angkor Night Market for budget souvenir shopping — silk scarves, wood carvings, and handmade jewelry. Enjoy dinner at a local Khmer restaurant away from the tourist strip for better prices.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-sunrise snack — pack fruit or bread from guesthouse the night before
meals.lunch: Temple complex food stall — rice with grilled chicken or fried noodles for $3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Local Khmer restaurant off the main strip — full meal for $3–5 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 2 liters of water. Temple dress code requires covered shoulders and knees. Start as early as possible to beat the heat and crowds. Your tuk-tuk driver will wait for you all day for a pre-agreed flat rate.

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 2 of your Angkor Pass to explore the lesser-visited outer temples. Visit Preah Khan — a sprawling jungle temple with atmospheric corridors and carvings. Then head to Neak Pean, a unique island temple surrounded by water, and Ta Som with its famous tree-covered eastern gopura.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pre Rup and East Mebon temples — excellent examples of classic Khmer pyramid temple architecture. Climb to the top of Pre Rup for panoramic views over the jungle. These temples are far less crowded than Angkor Wat and equally impressive.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset view from Phnom Bakheng hill temple (arrive by 4:30 PM as it gets crowded). Return to Siem Reap for a relaxing evening. Try a traditional Khmer cooking class at a local school — some offer budget classes for $10–15 USD including ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café — French toast with banana and honey for $2 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from guesthouse or local stall near temples — $2–3 USD
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner (if booked) or local restaurant — fish Amok or beef Lok Lak for $3–5 USD

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Bakheng has a visitor cap of 300 people at sunset — arrive early to secure a spot. Bring your Angkor Pass everywhere as rangers check tickets at each temple entrance. Rent a bicycle from your guesthouse ($2–3/day) to explore outer temples independently and save on tuk-tuk costs.

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 3 of your Angkor Pass for the remote Banteay Srei temple — known as the 'Jewel of Khmer Art' for its intricate pink sandstone carvings. Located about 25 km north of Siem Reap, hire a tuk-tuk for $20–25 USD for the day trip. Also visit the nearby Banteay Samré temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Landmine Museum on the way back — a sobering and important cultural site documenting Cambodia's landmine crisis, run by a former child soldier. Entrance by donation. Return to Siem Reap and visit the Artisans Angkor workshop — free entry, watch craftspeople create traditional Khmer silk and stone carvings.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your last evening in Siem Reap exploring the floating village of Kompong Phluk on Tonle Sap Lake (arrange a late afternoon boat tour for $15–20 USD). Watch the sunset over the lake. Enjoy a farewell Siem Reap dinner at a popular local spot.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near guesthouse — croissant and coffee for $2 USD
meals.lunch: Village restaurant near Banteay Srei — local Khmer set meal for $3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Siem Reap local restaurant — full Khmer feast with Amok, spring rolls, and iced tea for $5–7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is a must-see but requires early arrival to avoid tour groups. The Tonle Sap boat tour is best at late afternoon for golden-hour light. Bargain politely for tuk-tuk rates. Pack up your bags tonight as you'll be heading back toward the coast tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus or shared van back toward the coast — either to Sihanoukville, Kampot, or Kep depending on resort location. Journey takes 6–9 hours from Siem Reap ($10–15 USD). Enjoy the scenic Cambodian countryside. Arrive by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort area. Spend the afternoon unwinding on the beach — swim in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters, relax under a palm tree, and decompress from the busy temple-touring days. Explore any nearby coastal villages by foot or bicycle.
day_by_day.evening: If near Kampot — take a sunset boat cruise on the Kampot River ($5–8 USD per person, very popular with budget travelers). Watch fireflies along the riverbanks after dark. Enjoy a relaxed seafood dinner at a riverside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Bus station or guesthouse — Khmer porridge or fried rice for $1.50–2 USD
meals.lunch: Roadside stop during bus journey — packed snacks or noodle soup for $2 USD
meals.dinner: Riverside or beachside restaurant — fresh Kampot pepper crab or grilled fish for $5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is famous for its world-renowned Kampot pepper — try pepper crab or pepper steak at a local restaurant. The town has a charming French colonial architecture. If near Kep, the Kep Crab Market is legendary and very affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort or a local café. Take one last beach walk and swim. If near Kep, visit the Kep National Park for a short jungle hike with sea views ($1 USD entrance). If near Kampot, visit the famous Bokor Hill Station ruins for panoramic coastal views (hire a motorbike taxi for $10–15 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the final afternoon souvenir shopping at a local market — pick up Kampot pepper, silk scarves, handmade jewelry, and Angkor Wat-themed crafts as gifts. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Arrange airport transfer in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered during your trip. Reflect on 10 incredible days of Cambodian history, culture, and beaches. Head to the airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your flight.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local café — full Khmer breakfast with eggs, bread, and fruit for $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Local market food stall — Num Banh Chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry) for $1–2 USD
meals.dinner: Best local restaurant of the trip — splurge slightly on a farewell meal for $7–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Keep some USD for airport departure tax if not included in your ticket. Double-check your flight time and allow extra time for check-in. Cambodia has been an incredible destination — consider leaving a positive review for your guesthouse hosts who work hard for very little. Total estimated 10-day budget: $300–450 USD including accommodation, transport, food, and entrance fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable - travel day
meals.lunch: Not applicable - travel day
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival if available, or grab a quick bite at the airport before departure

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at 22:30. Keep Day 1 light. Confirm transfer arrangements in advance. Have local currency (Cambodian Riel or USD) ready for tips and incidentals. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Rest well for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast at the resort, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront to orient yourself with the surroundings. Explore the immediate resort area and nearby beach, dip your toes in the Gulf of Thailand or South China Sea, and enjoy the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local town or village market for a gentle introduction to Cambodian daily life. Browse fresh produce, local handicrafts, and street snacks. Chat with friendly vendors and pick up a few souvenirs or local spices. Return to the resort for a late afternoon swim or lounging by the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset stroll along the beach. Watch the sun dip below the horizon from the shoreline. Head to a nearby beachfront restaurant or the resort's dining area for a relaxed dinner with fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort - enjoy tropical fruits, eggs, and local Cambodian rice porridge (Bobor)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside cafe near the resort - try fresh spring rolls and a cold Angkor beer (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood dinner at a local restaurant near the resort - grilled fish, steamed crab, and jasmine rice (~$12-18 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Do not over-schedule. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen - November in Cambodia can still be warm and sunny. Exchange currency if needed at a local bank or ATM.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for a day trip to a nearby historical or cultural landmark. If based in Sihanoukville or Kep area, visit the Kep National Park and explore jungle trails with ocean views. If near Kampot, head to Phnom Chhngok Cave Temple - an ancient Khmer cave sanctuary with impressive stalactites and a small Hindu shrine dating back to the 7th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploration of the Kampot or Kep region. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market, a beloved local institution where fishing families sell freshly caught crabs and seafood directly from their boats. Stroll through the ruins of old French colonial villas in Kep, remnants of Cambodia's colonial past and the Khmer Rouge era.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Freshen up and head out for dinner at a riverside or beachfront restaurant. Enjoy the peaceful evening ambiance with local music if available.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure - eggs, baguette with butter and jam (French colonial influence), and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Fresh Kampot pepper crab at Kep Crab Market - a must-try Cambodian delicacy (~$10-15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the resort area - try Lok Lak (stir-fried beef with lime pepper sauce) and steamed rice (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for the day trip - negotiate a full-day rate (~$25-35 USD). Kampot pepper is world-famous; buy some at the market as a souvenir. Carry water and insect repellent for cave and jungle visits.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip to a nearby island for a beach and snorkeling experience. From Sihanoukville, popular options include Koh Rong Samloem or Koh Ta Kiev - pristine islands with clear turquoise waters and white sand beaches. Depart by 9:00 AM to maximize island time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon snorkeling over coral reefs, swimming in crystal-clear waters, and relaxing on secluded beaches. Explore the island on foot along jungle paths if energy permits. Observe diverse marine life including colorful fish and sea turtles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon. Shower and relax at the resort. Enjoy a quiet dinner and reflect on the day's island adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the boat departure - rice porridge, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch on the island - fresh grilled fish, coconut rice, and tropical fruit at a beachside shack (~$8-12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or nearby eatery - Amok (coconut fish curry in banana leaf) with steamed rice (~$10-14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book island boat trips in advance through the resort or a local tour operator (~$15-25 USD round trip). Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkel gear (rentable on island), and a dry bag for valuables. Check sea conditions - November can occasionally bring short rain showers.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Phnom Penh - Cambodia's vibrant capital city. Arrange a private taxi or bus transfer from the resort area (approximately 3-5 hours depending on starting point). Enjoy the scenic countryside drive through rice paddies and rural villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range hotel in Phnom Penh (pre-booked). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex - the stunning official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring Khmer architecture, sacred Buddha statues, and beautifully manicured gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay (Riverside Promenade) as the sun sets over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. Browse street vendors, watch locals exercising and socializing, and soak in the lively city atmosphere. Explore the FCC (Foreign Correspondents' Club) area for a drink with a river view.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant en route to Phnom Penh - try Bai Sach Chrouk (pork and rice) or a local noodle soup (~$3-5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh - try Khmer cuisine sampler platter with fish curry, stir-fried morning glory, and sticky rice (~$12-16 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book Phnom Penh accommodation in advance. Giant Ibis or Mekong Express buses offer comfortable mid-range transport (~$10-15 USD). The Royal Palace closes for lunch (11:30 AM - 2:00 PM); plan arrival accordingly. Entrance fee approximately $10 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) - a deeply moving and important historical site that was a Khmer Rouge detention and torture center during the 1975-1979 genocide. This sobering museum provides essential context for understanding modern Cambodian history. Allow 2-3 hours for a respectful and thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) approximately 15km outside the city. This memorial site includes a Buddhist stupa filled with victims' skulls and bones, and audio guide tours that tell powerful personal stories. Afterward, visit the National Museum of Cambodia near the Royal Palace to see the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Recover emotionally with a peaceful evening. Visit Wat Phnom - the hilltop temple that gives the city its name - for a tranquil sunset moment. Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for evening shopping and street food.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Phnom Penh hotel or a nearby French-style bakery - baguette, croissant, and cafe au lait (colonial influence, ~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch near the National Museum - try a local Khmer restaurant for beef noodle soup (Kuy Teav) or rice with grilled pork (~$4-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-regarded mid-range Khmer restaurant - sample a full traditional Cambodian meal with multiple dishes (~$15-20 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally heavy sites. Take breaks as needed and be respectful of the solemnity of these places. Entry to Tuol Sleng ~$5 USD, Choeung Ek ~$6 USD with audio guide. Dress modestly. The National Museum charges ~$10 USD entry.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Siem Reap - gateway to the magnificent Angkor temple complex. Take a comfortable bus or domestic flight (recommended for time efficiency). The bus journey takes approximately 6 hours; a flight takes 45 minutes (~$40-80 USD). Check into a mid-range hotel in Siem Reap.
day_by_day.afternoon: After arriving and checking in, visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap town - an excellent introduction to Angkor's history and the Khmer Empire before visiting the temples. The museum provides rich context that will greatly enhance your temple visits over the following days.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Siem Reap's vibrant Pub Street and Old Market (Phsar Chas) area. Browse souvenir shops, silk scarves, and local crafts. Enjoy the lively street atmosphere with traditional Apsara dance performances at nearby restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Phnom Penh hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a roadside stop - packed lunch or local restaurant (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner on Pub Street in Siem Reap - try a restaurant offering traditional Apsara dance performance with Khmer set menu (~$15-25 USD including show)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus or flight to Siem Reap in advance. Giant Ibis and Mekong Express are reliable bus options. Purchase your Angkor Archaeological Park pass in advance or on arrival - a 3-day pass costs $62 USD and is highly recommended for your stay. The museum entry is ~$12 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn (4:30 AM wake-up) for the iconic sunrise at Angkor Wat - one of the world's most breathtaking experiences. Watch the sun rise over the world's largest religious monument, reflected in the lotus ponds. Explore Angkor Wat's outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting Hindu epics, and towering central towers as the light gradually illuminates the ancient stone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Bayon Temple at Angkor Thom - famous for its 216 massive stone faces of Avalokitesvara smiling serenely in all directions. Explore the Elephant Terrace, the Terrace of the Leper King, and the Baphuon temple. Visit Ta Prohm - the atmospheric 'Tomb Raider' temple where massive silk-cotton trees dramatically engulf ancient stone structures.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap by late afternoon. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage to soothe tired muscles (~$12-18 USD for 1 hour). Dinner and relaxation in town.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed breakfast or energy bars before the sunrise visit; grab a proper breakfast near Angkor Wat from food stalls after sunrise (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the restaurants near the Angkor complex - try Khmer noodles or fried rice with vegetables (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Siem Reap restaurant - try Khmer red curry with chicken, eggplant, and jasmine rice (~$10-14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a knowledgeable local tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$20-25 USD) - they know the best routes and timing. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and comfortable walking shoes. Dress respectfully (shoulders and knees covered) for all temple visits. The Angkor complex is vast - pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the outer temples of the Angkor Archaeological Park. Visit Banteay Srei - the 'Citadel of Women' - renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in all of Khmer art. Located about 25km from Siem Reap, this smaller temple rewards close inspection of its delicate floral motifs and mythological scenes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Samre - a beautifully preserved Angkor-era temple less visited by tourists, offering a more intimate experience. Then explore Preah Khan - a sprawling jungle temple with long atmospheric corridors, carved nagas, and a fascinating mix of Buddhist and Hindu iconography. Enjoy the quieter atmosphere compared to the main Angkor circuit.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the floating villages on Tonle Sap Lake - the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. A boat tour through the stilted villages and floating schools offers a fascinating glimpse into a unique way of life. Watch the sunset over the vast lake.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Siem Reap hotel - Cambodian-style with rice soup, fried egg, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near Banteay Srei or at a local restaurant in the area - fresh baguette sandwiches and fruit (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell Siem Reap dinner at a well-regarded restaurant - try a full Khmer tasting menu with Amok, Lok Lak, and fresh coconut dessert (~$15-20 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a longer tuk-tuk ride - negotiate a full-day rate (~$30-35 USD). The Tonle Sap boat tour costs approximately $10-15 USD. November marks the end of the wet season, so the lake is at its fullest and most impressive. Bring a light jacket for the boat ride as it can be breezy on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cambodia. If time permits before checkout, visit the Siem Reap Artisans Angkor workshop and shop - a social enterprise employing disadvantaged Cambodians to revive traditional Khmer craftsmanship in silk weaving, lacquerware, and stone carving. Free guided tours of the workshop are available and highly informative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Old Market (Phsar Chas) - pick up silk scarves, silver jewelry, Kampot pepper, coconut palm sugar, and handmade crafts. Visit a local cafe for a final cup of Cambodian coffee (strong, sweet, and served over ice). Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Siem Reap International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on 10 incredible days exploring Cambodia's beaches, history, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast - enjoy a full spread of Cambodian and Western options
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Siem Reap cafe - try a Khmer sandwich (nom pang) with pate, pickled vegetables, and herbs (~$2-4 USD) - a perfect final taste of Cambodia
meals.dinner: Airport dining or early dinner before departure - light meal at an airport restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some USD for airport taxes or last-minute purchases. Artisans Angkor purchases support local communities and make excellent authentic souvenirs. Confirm your return flight details the night before. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be arranged to whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a warm welcome with a complimentary late-night refreshment and a brief resort orientation from your personal butler.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — travel day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — travel day
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and champagne arranged by the resort upon arrival — chilled tropical fruits, artisan cheeses, and Cambodian finger foods served in your villa.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your private airport transfer is pre-booked through the resort concierge. Request early check-in amenities such as a warm towel service and turndown. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority after a long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort morning. Take a sunrise stroll along the private beachfront of Aegean Bliss Resort, breathing in the coastal air. Indulge in a 90-minute traditional Khmer massage at the resort's luxury spa to ease jet lag and rejuvenate after travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate coastal surroundings with a guided resort boat tour along the shoreline. Discover hidden coves, observe local fishing villages from the water, and snorkel in the crystal-clear Cambodian waters near the resort's private pier. Equipment and a certified guide are provided.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private sunset cocktail session on the resort's overwater deck. Watch the golden Cambodian sun dip below the Gulf of Thailand horizon. Transition to the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant for a curated dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast buffet at the resort's beachfront restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), eggs Benedict, freshly baked croissants, and freshly squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's cabana bar — grilled tiger prawns, green papaya salad, and coconut-chilled beverages.
meals.dinner: Seven-course tasting menu at the resort's flagship restaurant featuring locally sourced Cambodian seafood, Khmer-spiced lobster, and premium wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: November in Cambodia offers excellent weather — warm, dry, and breezy along the coast. This is the start of the high season, making it ideal for beach and water activities. Confirm spa appointments at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by private luxury charter flight or helicopter transfer to Siem Reap — the gateway to the ancient Angkor Archaeological Park. Upon arrival, check in briefly at a luxury day-use suite at a premium Siem Reap hotel (e.g., Amansara or Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor). Begin your Angkor exploration with a private guided tour of Angkor Wat at dawn — witness the sunrise reflecting on the iconic temple moat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Angkor circuit with a private Egyptologist-style historian guide. Visit the enigmatic Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the jungle-draped Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider' temple), and the royal terraces of the Elephant and Leper King. Travel by air-conditioned private tuk-tuk or luxury SUV between sites.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town for a cultural evening. Attend a private Apsara dance performance — Cambodia's UNESCO-recognized classical dance form — hosted in a heritage villa setting. Dine at a premium Siem Reap restaurant afterward.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-dawn breakfast box prepared by the resort — croissants, fruit, coffee thermos, and energy bars for the sunrise temple visit.
meals.lunch: Elegant al fresco lunch at a boutique Siem Reap restaurant — Amok fish curry, lok lak beef, and fresh coconut water served in a shaded garden setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or equivalent premium Khmer fine-dining restaurant — modern Cambodian tasting menu highlighting heirloom ingredients and regional flavors.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for temple visits — shoulders and knees must be covered. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and comfortable walking shoes. The Angkor Archaeological Park pass (3-day recommended) should be arranged in advance through your concierge. Return flight or transfer back to the resort can be arranged for late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Siem Reap (if overnight stay was arranged) or continue from resort. Morning visit to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — a stunning 10th-century temple renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest in all of Angkor. Travel with a private art historian guide who contextualizes the mythology and craftsmanship.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum for a deep-dive into Khmer civilization history, featuring galleries of golden artifacts, ancient inscriptions, and multimedia presentations. Afterward, explore the Artisans Angkor workshop — a social enterprise preserving traditional Cambodian silk weaving, lacquerware, and stone carving. Browse and purchase premium handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Observe floating villages, local life on the water, and the dramatic Cambodian sky at dusk. Return to Siem Reap for a private rooftop dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at your Siem Reap luxury hotel — Cambodian congee, French pastries, tropical fruit platters, and specialty Cambodian coffee.
meals.lunch: Private picnic lunch arranged by your guide near Banteay Srei — gourmet Cambodian wraps, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages in a shaded temple garden.
meals.dinner: Rooftop dinner at a premium Siem Reap establishment — whole grilled barramundi, Khmer red curry, and imported wine selection with panoramic town views.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is approximately 25km from central Siem Reap — factor in travel time. The Tonlé Sap boat cruise is best experienced during November when water levels are still high from monsoon season. Confirm boat arrangements through your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer or flight back to the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront. Upon return, enjoy a restorative morning at the resort's infinity pool overlooking the sea. Participate in a guided morning yoga session on the beach led by a certified instructor — a perfect blend of wellness and natural surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a private island-hopping excursion by chartered speedboat to nearby uninhabited islands. Snorkel in vibrant coral reefs, explore white sand beaches, and enjoy a champagne picnic on a secluded sandbar. The resort's marine biologist guide will introduce you to the local marine ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private beachside bonfire dinner experience. Tables set directly on the sand, illuminated by lanterns and torches. A personal chef prepares a live seafood BBQ with freshly caught lobster, prawns, and fish.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before transfer — fresh smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and cold brew coffee.
meals.lunch: Champagne picnic on a private sandbar — charcuterie boards, fresh tropical fruits, artisan bread, and chilled Moët & Chandon.
meals.dinner: Private beachside BBQ dinner — whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, catch-of-the-day fish, grilled vegetables, and a curated Cambodian dessert spread including sticky rice with mango.

day_by_day.notes: November sea conditions are generally calm and ideal for island hopping. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only to protect the coral ecosystem. The private island excursion should be booked through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Phnom Penh — Cambodia's vibrant capital city — by chartered flight or premium road transfer. Begin with a sobering but essential historical visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison), guided by a private historian who provides thoughtful, respectful context to Cambodia's Khmer Rouge history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields Memorial) — a deeply moving and important historical site. Afterward, decompress with a visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a gleaming complex of Khmer royal architecture, sacred Buddha statues, and manicured gardens. Explore with a certified royal palace guide.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Phnom Penh Riverside promenade at sunset — a lively boulevard flanked by colonial-era buildings, local vendors, and the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers. Enjoy a premium dinner in a colonial heritage building.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or en route — Cambodian rice soup with ginger, freshly baked baguette (a French colonial legacy), and Cambodian iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Malis Restaurant Phnom Penh or equivalent — refined Cambodian cuisine in a garden setting, featuring signature Khmer dishes with modern presentation.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant or equivalent fine-dining establishment — French-Cambodian fusion cuisine, premium wine list, and elegant colonial ambiance.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally intense — allow time for reflection. Photography is permitted in certain areas with sensitivity. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees) for the Royal Palace visit. A premium overnight stay at Raffles Hotel Le Royal Phnom Penh is recommended for this night.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Cambodia — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture, housed in a stunning terracotta pavilion. A private curator-led tour provides unparalleled insight into Cambodian artistic heritage from the pre-Angkorian era to the present.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — Phnom Penh's iconic Art Deco market dome. Browse luxury Cambodian silk scarves, silver jewelry, and gemstones with a personal shopping guide who helps you identify authentic, high-quality pieces. Visit a premium silk boutique for bespoke fabric selections.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails aboard a private luxury river cruise on the Mekong River — sipping signature cocktails while watching the golden light play across the water and the city skyline. Disembark for a farewell Phnom Penh dinner before transferring back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Raffles Hotel Le Royal — lavish colonial-era buffet with Cambodian, Asian, and Western options, freshly squeezed juices, and specialty coffees.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium riverside restaurant — Cambodian-style steamed fish in banana leaf, amok curry, and fresh coconut desserts.
meals.dinner: Farewell Phnom Penh dinner at Khéma Restaurant or equivalent — French bistro classics with Cambodian ingredients, accompanied by a curated Bordeaux wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transfer back to the resort following dinner, or consider an overnight return by luxury sleeper vehicle if preferred. The Mekong river cruise should be booked in advance and typically runs 1.5 to 2 hours. Silk purchases at the market can be shipped internationally through premium courier services.

day_by_day.morning: Full wellness and relaxation day at Aegean Bliss Resort. Begin with a private sunrise meditation session on the beach with a resident wellness guru. Follow with a comprehensive 3-hour Royal Khmer Spa Journey — including a traditional herbal compress massage, a coconut milk body scrub, and a rejuvenating facial using local botanical ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a private Cambodian cooking class hosted by the resort's executive chef. Learn to prepare authentic Khmer dishes — fish amok, lok lak, nom banh chok (Khmer noodles), and traditional palm sugar desserts. Use fresh ingredients sourced from local markets and the resort's herb garden.
day_by_day.evening: Dine on the dishes you prepared in your cooking class at a private candlelit table on your villa's terrace. The resort sommelier pairs each course with selected wines and Cambodian craft spirits. A live traditional Cambodian music duo performs softly in the background.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast service — tropical fruit platter, eggs cooked to order, Cambodian rice porridge, freshly baked pastries, and specialty coffee delivered to your private terrace.
meals.lunch: Light spa-inspired lunch at the wellness center — cold-pressed juices, grain bowls, grilled vegetables, and herbal teas.
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dinner featuring dishes prepared in your cooking class — fish amok, lok lak, fresh spring rolls, and coconut sticky rice dessert with paired wines.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically accommodates up to 4 guests and lasts approximately 3 hours including the meal. Inform the chef of any dietary restrictions or allergies in advance. This day is designed as a restorative interlude between cultural excursions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private chartered boat excursion to Koh Rong or Koh Rong Sanloem island — among Cambodia's most pristine and beautiful islands. Arrive early to enjoy the beaches before day-trippers arrive. Explore bioluminescent plankton bays (visible at night), dense jungle interiors via a guided nature walk, and vibrant underwater coral gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on a secluded beach cove accessible only by boat — swim in turquoise waters, lounge on powdery white sand, and enjoy water sports including kayaking and paddleboarding. Your private boat crew serves refreshments throughout the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort as the sun sets over the Gulf of Thailand. Freshen up and enjoy a premium cocktail hour at the resort bar featuring Cambodian-inspired cocktails — lemongrass mojitos, tamarind sours, and palm sugar daiquiris. Dinner at the resort's seafood terrace.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with fresh fruits, pastries, yogurt, and strong Cambodian coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the private island beach — prepared by the resort chef and delivered in a luxury hamper: lobster rolls, tropical fruit salad, artisan cheeses, and chilled rosé wine.
meals.dinner: Seafood terrace dinner at the resort — whole steamed crab, grilled scallops, Cambodian-style sautéed squid, and a premium seafood platter for two with chilled white Burgundy.

day_by_day.notes: The island excursion requires an early morning departure (typically 7:00–8:00 AM) to maximize time on the island. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light rash guard, and insect repellent for the jungle walk. The bioluminescent bay experience is best after 9 PM if you choose to stay for the evening — confirm logistics with the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — savor every last moment. Wake up for a private sunrise beach walk with a resort naturalist who identifies coastal birds, shells, and marine life. Return for a final indulgent spa treatment — a 60-minute hot stone massage and a revitalizing scalp treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely checkout experience — the resort offers a late checkout (subject to availability, typically 2:00–3:00 PM for premium guests). Spend the remaining time at the infinity pool, sipping farewell cocktails and reflecting on the journey. Browse the resort's boutique for premium Cambodian artisan gifts, silk items, and locally made wellness products.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport for your departure flight. The resort concierge arranges a seamless departure experience including luggage handling, airport fast-track service, and a farewell gift hamper filled with Cambodian specialty teas, artisan chocolates, and a handwoven silk keepsake.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant — a full spread of your favorite dishes from the trip, plus a special Cambodian breakfast platter curated by the chef as a final culinary memory.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the poolside cabana — fresh salads, grilled fish tacos, and tropical smoothies.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport's premium lounge or en route depending on flight schedule — the resort can arrange a gourmet departure meal box if the flight departs in the early evening.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late checkout at least 48 hours prior with the resort concierge. Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure flight for airport check-in and security. The resort farewell gift hamper is a complimentary luxury touch — confirm with your butler the day before departure. Ensure all purchased items, including fragile ceramics or silk, are properly packaged for travel.
